incident_spec.summary: High percentage of temporary tables created on disk in MySQL.
symptoms: 30% of temporary tables created on disk despite configuration changes.
Observed behavior persists even after increasing `tmp_table_size` and `max_heap_table_size`.
Another system with the same database shows only 1% of temporary tables created on disk.
incident_spec.mechanism: MySQL creates temporary tables on disk when certain conditions are met, such as the presence of TEXT/BLOB fields, large column sizes, or exceeding memory limits for temporary tables.

facts.evidence: The DBA explicitly mentioned increasing these parameters to reduce disk-based temporary tables.

facts.key: 30% of temporary tables created on disk
facts.evidence: The DBA observed this percentage after configuration changes.

facts.key: TEXT/BLOB fields and large columns can trigger disk-based temporary tables
facts.evidence: The DBA and answer authors discussed this as a potential cause.

assumptions: The database schema includes TEXT/BLOB fields or large columns.
